title: Series of edge-sharing bi-triangle Ln4 clusters with a μ4-NO3− bridge: syntheses, structures, luminescence, and the SMM behavior of the Dy4 analogue

material_class.structural_family: edge-sharing bi-triangle Ln4 cluster with μ4-NO3− bridge

synthesis.procedure: A mixture of Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (1.0 mmol, 0.451 g), o-vanillin (0.5 mmol, 0.0761 g), 2-(2-aminoethoxy)ethanol (0.5 mmol, 0.0526 g), and triethylamine (0.2 mmol) in 16 mL MeOH–MeCN (v:v = 3:1) was stirred at room temperature for 20 min, then heated to 80 °C and stirred for 30 min. The yellow solution was left unperturbed at room temperature for slow evaporation; yellow block crystals formed after five days. The Schiff-base ligand L formed in situ.
synthesis.temperature: room temperature 20 min, then 80 °C 30 min; crystallization at room temperature
synthesis.time: stir 20 min then 30 min; crystals after five days
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction followed by slow evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: yellow solution left unperturbed for slow solvent evaporation; yellow block single crystals after five days

properties.summary: Dc susceptibility of 1 shows χmT = 31.55 cm3 K mol−1 at 300 K (expected 31.50 for four spin-only GdIII), nearly constant until a small drop below 18 K to 29.51 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K, indicating very weak antiferromagnetic Gd···Gd coupling. Magnetization at 2 K saturates at 27.88 Nβ above 2 T, consistent with an isotropic system. No slow magnetization relaxation under zero dc field.

material_class.structural_family: edge-sharing bi-triangle Ln4 cluster with μ4-NO3− bridge

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by the same procedure as 1, substituting Tb(NO3)3·6H2O for Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (1.0 mmol Gd salt, 0.5 mmol o-vanillin, 0.5 mmol 2-(2-aminoethoxy)ethanol, 0.2 mmol triethylamine, 16 mL MeOH–MeCN 3:1, stir 20 min at room temperature then 30 min at 80 °C; slow evaporation).

reagents.name: terbium(III) nitrate hexahydrate
reagents.amount: used in place of 1.0 mmol Gd(NO3)3·6H2O

synthesis.temperature: room temperature then 80 °C; crystallization at room temperature
synthesis.time: stir 20 min then 30 min; crystals after five days (as in 1)
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: slow evaporation of the yellow solution as for 1

properties.summary: Solid-state luminescence of 2 (the only emissive analogue) shows green TbIII emission under 332 nm excitation at 293 K (similar at 77 K) with peaks at 488, 542, 586 and 622 nm (5D4 → 7FJ, J = 6–3). Magnetically, χmT of 2–6 follows thermal depopulation of Ln Stark levels; reduced magnetization of 2 is not superposed, indicating anisotropy. No SMM slow relaxation under zero dc field.

synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: slow evaporation of the yellow solution as for 1

properties.summary: χmT of 3 is 57.4 cm3 K mol−1 at 300 K (expected 56.7 for four uncoupled DyIII) and decreases to 25.5 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K, mainly from depopulation of Dy Stark levels. Magnetization at 2 K approaches 22.1 μB (well below 40 μB) with non-superposed M vs H/T, indicating anisotropy; a narrow hysteresis is noted at 2 K. Zero-field ac susceptibility is frequency-dependent below 8 K (SMM). Cole–Cole α = 0.18–0.32. Arrhenius fit above 5 K gives Ueff = 28 K and τ0 = 1.7 × 10−7 s.

properties.summary: Dc χmT of 4 follows the same thermal evolution as the other anisotropic analogues, attributed to depopulation of HoIII Stark levels and very weak coupling. Reduced magnetization curves are not superposed. No zero-field slow relaxation (SMM) was observed.
